question: Who among the following defeated Mughal emperor Humayun in the Battle of Kannauj in 1540?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher Shah Suri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sher Shah Suri was the founder of the Sur Empire in North India, which ruled from 1540 to 1555.
 
• The Battle of Kannauj, also known as the Battle of Bilgram, was fought on 17 May 1540 between Sher Shah Suri and Mughal Emperor Humayun.
 
• Humayun was decisively defeated by Sher Shah Suri, leading to the temporary displacement of the Mughal Empire.
 
• This victory allowed Sher Shah Suri to establish control over the Mughal territories, solidifying his power in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Humayun**

 
 
• Humayun was the second emperor of the Mughal Empire, ruling from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.
 
• He was the son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire.
 
• After his defeat at the hands of Sher Shah Suri, Humayun went into exile and sought refuge in Persia.
 
• Humayun eventually regained his throne in 1555 with the help of Persian forces but died shortly after in 1556.
 
 
 
• **Sur Empire**
 
 
• The Sur Empire was established by Sher Shah Suri after defeating Humayun in 1540.
 
• It marked a brief interruption in the Mughal rule over North India.
 
• Sher Shah Suri is known for his administrative reforms and for building the Grand Trunk Road, which still exists today.
 
• The Sur Empire lasted until 1555 when the Mughals regained control under Humayun.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Chausa**
 
 
• The Battle of Chausa was fought in 1539 between Sher Shah Suri and Humayun.
 
• Sher Shah Suri emerged victorious in this battle, which was a precursor to the Battle of Kannauj.
 
• This defeat weakened Humayun's position and paved the way for Sher Shah Suri's eventual dominance.
 
 
 
• **Military Reforms of Sher Shah Suri**
 
 
• Sher Shah Suri is known for his significant military reforms, including the introduction of a new administrative system for his army.
 
• He introduced the concept of branding horses to prevent corruption and ensure the quality of his cavalry.
 
• Sher Shah's military efficiency played a crucial role in his victories against the Mughals.
